title: Quick questions before I design this
lede: A place where recent and soon-to-be grads pick a career area, find a professional in it, and get advice (with helpers able to earn for their time). It should feel social and fun, but clean and simpler than LinkedIn.

questions.title: Phone or computer first?
questions.why: Your answers picked a phone app, but your description says to start with a web app. The layout changes a lot between the two.

options.label: Phone
options.detail: Designed for a phone held in one hand

options.label: Web, on a computer
options.detail: A wider screen, more visible at once

questions.title: Which moment of the starting page should I show?
questions.why: You described two clicks: pick an area of interest, then pick a professional. I can show either step, or both on one screen.

options.label: Both on one screen
options.detail: Areas at the top, professionals below update as you pick

options.label: Picking an area
options.detail: The very first thing a student sees

questions.title: What should it feel like?
questions.why: You said social and fun but clean. These help me find where between those it should sit.
questions.textPlaceholder: e.g. Like texting a friend's older sibling for advice

questions.title: How visible should paying for help be on this page?
questions.why: Helpers can get paid. Showing prices up front sets expectations; hiding them keeps the first page friendlier.

options.label: Show a price or 'free' on each person

questions.title: How many directions should I design?
questions.why: More directions, more range; fewer, faster to compare.

questions.title: Anything fixed or off-limits?
questions.why: Optional. A product name, a color you love or hate, or a look you never want.
questions.placeholder: e.g. It's called Bridge, and please no navy and gold
